name: KNSCHA-rvt_RVT100UF16V67RV0016
title: RVT series SMD aluminium electrolytic capacitor, 100 µF 16 V, 6.3 × 5.4 mm, 105 °C 2000 h
summary: RVT100UF16V67RV0016 is a surface-mount (V-chip) aluminium electrolytic capacitor of the RVT series: 100 µF, 16 V rated, ±20 %, in a 6.3 mm diameter by 5.4 mm tall can on a resin seat plate. It is rated from -55 °C to +105 °C with an endurance of 2000 hours at 105 °C under rated voltage, and carries 63 mA rms of ripple at 105 °C, 120 Hz. The part is polarised and RoHS compliant.

operation.text: The series follows JIS C-5141 (characteristic W) and JIS C-5101 unless a figure says otherwise, and meets RoHS directive 2011/65/EU. Taping follows JIS C0806.

The can top carries the series name (RVT), the rated voltage, the capacitance in µF and a dark band over the negative side. The reel label gives voltage and capacitance, series, lot number, quantity and, on request, the customer part number.

The capacitor is polar: neither reverse nor AC voltage may be applied, and a circuit where the polarity can flip needs a bipolar type, which is still unsuitable for pure AC. DC bias plus ripple peak must stay at or below the rated voltage. Two or more in series need a total below the summed rating and a balancing resistor across each so they share voltage evenly.

Ambient temperature and ripple current must stay inside the rated figures, and the endurance rating should match the product's required life. Circuits with fast, frequent charge and discharge call for a purpose-built long-life capacitor instead.

Not for use where the part meets water, condensation, brine or oil; toxic gases such as hydrogen sulfide, sulfurous or nitrous acid, chlorine, bromine, methyl bromide or ammonia; ozone, ultraviolet light or radiation; or vibration and shock beyond the rating. Vibration rating: 10-55-10 Hz logarithmic sweep at one sweep per minute, 1.5 mm amplitude (10 G max), 2 h in each of X, Y and Z. Shock is normally not rated.

Electrolyte and separator are combustible and the electrolyte conducts, so a leak can corrode copper or short traces; keep traces out from under the sealed end. Keep heat-producing parts away from the capacitor, including directly beneath it on the far side of the board. On double-sided boards avoid placing it over unneeded holes and vias. Characteristics shift with temperature and frequency, and parallel units need attention to how current divides between them.

Use infrared or hot-air reflow; vapour-phase heating is not recommended. Reflow once; if a second pass is needed, leave at least 30 minutes between passes. With infrared heating the absorbed heat depends on body colour and size.

Check rating and polarity before placing. Do not reuse a part once it has been mounted and powered, and discard any part that has been dropped. Avoid deforming the body and watch for impact from placement nozzles, checkers and centring jaws. After soldering, do not tilt or twist the body, lift the board by the capacitor, let other boards or parts press on it, or expose it to radiant heat from nearby hot parts.

Halogenated cleaners need KNSCHA's approval, and ozone-depleting agents should be avoided. Any type and rating may be cleaned by immersion, ultrasonic or similar methods for no more than 2 minutes in total, with the agent at 40 ℃ or below, then dried with the board in hot air for at least 10 minutes at a temperature no higher than the maximum operating temperature. Poor drying after a water rinse can swell the seat plate.

Do not touch the terminals, bridge them with a conductor, or let acid, alkali or other conducting liquid reach the part. Capacitors in industrial equipment should be inspected periodically for an opened vent or leaking electrolyte and for capacitance, dissipation factor and leakage current. If the vent releases smoke, switch off or unplug the equipment; wash mouth and throat with water after inhaling the gas or swallowing electrolyte, and wash skin with soap and water.

Store indoors at 5 ℃ to 35 ℃ and below 75 % relative humidity, away from water, brine, oil, ozone, ultraviolet light and radiation. After more than 2 years of storage the leakage current can rise; if it has, recondition the part by applying voltage through a 1 kΩ resistor.
Crush the capacitor or pierce its body before incineration; where burning is not possible, pass it to a waste contractor for landfill.
